cells.label: ironRam

sheets.title: Ally and projectiles
sheets.brief: The cavalry ally plus every projectile kind. Two of the rounds are live effects and cannot be bitmaps.

cells.label: cavalry
cells.note: Reference only — the rider is adopted as a GALLOP STRIP from walk-cavalry, not as a still. Cool blue, gold pennant, facing right. Must stay unmistakable against the warm-toned enemies at a glance.

cells.label: arrow
cells.note: The most-fired round in the game — the archer post and both bolt-throwing ships.

cells.label: quarrel
cells.note: The siege ballista’s round, and the one shot the player has to see coming and answer.

cells.label: ball
cells.note: Cannonball. No override hook: this one is drawn from its own geometry every frame.

cells.label: shell
cells.note: Mortar shell — finned, fuse lit, points along its arc. No override hook: this one is drawn from its own geometry every frame.

cells.label: bomb
cells.note: Enemy ordnance, nose-down along its fall. No override hook: this one is drawn from its own geometry every frame.

cells.label: fire
cells.note: Molotov, tumbling. No override hook: this one is drawn from its own geometry every frame.

cells.label: frost
cells.note: The frost round is a live particle emitter; this is only its core shard.

sheets.title: Props, sky bodies and shipped UI
sheets.brief: The discrete background objects and the four bitmaps that already ship. The tileable parallax bands are deliberately absent — they need a strip, not a grid.

cells.label: conifer
cells.note: Stacked canopy tiers with a lit right edge. Reads at 30 px in a parallax band, so silhouette over detail.

cells.label: broadleaf
cells.note: The other half of the tree line. Must not read as the conifer at distance.

cells.label: sun
cells.note: Disc plus its ray fan. The wide bloom wash across the sky and the dawn/day/dusk tinting are painted around this, not into it, so they stay procedural.

cells.label: moon
cells.note: Cratered disc, no rays. Identical at every wave tier — the blood moon is the SKY going red behind it, not the moon itself.
